# 1 Clement Chapter 51 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 51 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_051_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 51

**51:1** Therefore whatever things we have transgressed, and whatever things we have done through the assaults of the adversary, let us ask that these may be forgiven us; and those too who set themselves up as leaders of rebellion and sedition ought to regard the common hope.

**51:2** For those who live in fear and love wish to have themselves fall into torments rather than their neighbors — and they would prefer to bear their own condemnation than to have the harmony that has been so nobly and righteously handed down to us defamed.

**51:3** For it is better for a man to confess his transgression than to harden his heart, as the heart of those was hardened who made rebellion against Moses the servant of God — whose judgment was manifest.

**51:4** For they went down into Hades alive, and "Death shall be their shepherd."

**51:5** Pharaoh and his host and all the leaders of Egypt, the chariots and their riders were drowned in the Red Sea and perished, for no other reason than that their foolish hearts were hardened after that the signs and wonders had been wrought in the land of Egypt through Moses the servant of God.

---

*EMET renders the Greek of Codex Alexandrinus with maximal literalness.*
